definition_one_sentence: A customer account with at least one non-cancelled order in the last 12 calendar months as of the reporting date.
formula_or_rule: Join fct_orders to stg_customers on customer_id. For reporting date D, count distinct registered customer_id where status <> 'cancelled' and order_date BETWEEN D - INTERVAL '12 months' AND D. Missing dates do not qualify.
example: Example only: on 2026-11-25, an account with a non-cancelled order on 2026-04-10 is active for the company but outside the Sales 6-month window.
notes_conflicts: CTP3 role-play decision. Finance uses 12 months and excludes cancelled orders. Sales uses the separate label recently active customer (6 months), with the same order rules and a 6-month window.

definition_one_sentence: Order revenue in euros after refunds and excluding VAT, with shipping included.
formula_or_rule: Per order: ROUND((gross_revenue_eur - refunded_eur) / 1.20, 2). Gross is orders.total_amount_eur. Refunds are SUM(payments.amount) where payment_status = 'refunded', or 0 when none exist.
example: Example only: for an order total of EUR 120.00 and refunds of EUR 24.00, net revenue = (120.00 - 24.00) / 1.20 = EUR 80.00.
notes_conflicts: CTP3 role-play decision. The lab assumes 20% VAT for every order. Shipping is already in the order total. Sales uses sales revenue including VAT = gross_revenue_eur - refunded_eur. The starter model uses order totals, not captured cash.

definition_one_sentence: A customer account that ordered before but has no non-cancelled order in the last 12 calendar months as of the reporting date.
formula_or_rule: For registered customer accounts and reporting date D, require at least one non-cancelled order dated on or before D, and none with order_date BETWEEN D - INTERVAL '12 months' AND D. Accounts with no dated non-cancelled order are not labelled churned.
example: Example only: on 2026-11-25, an account whose last non-cancelled order was on 2025-10-01 is churned. An account that never ordered is not churned.
notes_conflicts: CTP3 role-play decision. Use the company 12-month window. Do not treat a missing order date or a never-buyer as evidence of churn.

definition_one_sentence: A registered ShopFast account identified by customer_id, whether or not it has placed an order.
formula_or_rule: Count distinct customer_id in stg_customers after removing exact duplicate rows. Different account IDs remain different customers even if they share an email.
example: Example only: two copied rows with customer_id 10410 count as one customer. Two different customer IDs with the same email count as two accounts.
notes_conflicts: CTP3 role-play decision. The dataset identifies accounts, not unique people. A shared email is not enough to merge accounts.

definition_one_sentence: A purchase request identified by order_id, including pending, shipped, delivered, returned and cancelled requests.
formula_or_rule: Count distinct order_id in stg_orders. Keep one row per order_id after sorting by order_date. Include every status for an order count, then apply the separate non-cancelled rule for active customers.
example: Example only: two source rows with order_id 700001 count as one order. An order with status cancelled still counts as an order but does not make its customer active.
notes_conflicts: CTP3 role-play decision. An order is not the same as a captured payment. Payment records are stored separately in stg_payments.
